events.title_zh: 图灵发表《论可计算数》——计算机的理论蓝图
events.title_en: Turing's On Computable Numbers
events.summary_zh: 1936 年，艾伦·图灵发表《论可计算数及其在判定问题上的应用》。为了证明希尔伯特判定问题无解，他设想了一种假想机器——无限长纸带、读写头、简单规则表——这就是图灵机，所有现代计算机的抽象蓝图。
events.why_it_matters_zh: 这篇论文定义了「什么是计算」。图灵机是所有编程语言、操作系统和芯片架构的共同祖先。没有它你不仅没有 AI——你甚至没有电脑。
events.behind_scenes_zh:
图灵写这篇论文时才 24 岁。他的真正目标是解决希尔伯特 1928 年提出的判定问题——是否存在一种通用算法能判断任意数学命题的真假。图灵证明了答案是不能。
为了完成这个证明他必须先定义「算法到底是什么」，于是他发明了图灵机。整个计算机时代其实是这篇 36 页论文的一个副产品。
冯·诺依曼后来承认：计算机的核心概念——程序和数据共用存储——直接来自图灵机。
events.source_name: London Mathematical Society
events.learning_path_hint: 配合「可计算数」词典卡和图灵的「智能机器」1948 报告一起看。
events.card_summary_zh: 图灵为了回答“什么能被计算”，提出了图灵机，也意外画出了后来所有通用计算机的理论蓝图。
events.card_summary_en: Seeking to define what can be computed, Alan Turing proposed the Turing machine. This abstract mathematical model inadvertently established the theoretical blueprint for all general-purpose computers that followed.
events.summary_en: Alan Turing published "On Computable Numbers, with an Application to the Entscheidungsproblem," a landmark paper in theoretical computer science. To prove that David Hilbert's decision problem had no solution, Turing conceptualized a hypothetical device consisting of an infinitely long paper tape, a read/write head, and a simple table of rules. This conceptual device became known as the Turing machine. By formalizing the concept of algorithmic execution, Turing created the abstract blueprint for all modern computing architecture.
events.context_en: Turing was only 24 years old when he wrote this seminal 36-page paper. His primary objective was not to invent a machine, but to resolve the Entscheidungsproblem posed by David Hilbert in 1928, which asked whether a general algorithm could determine the truth or falsehood of any given mathematical statement. Turing proved that such an algorithm could not exist. However, to construct this mathematical proof, he first needed to rigorously define what an "algorithm" actually was. His solution was the invention of the Turing machine. Consequently, the foundational architecture of the entire computer age emerged as a byproduct of this theoretical mathematics paper. John von Neumann later acknowledged that the core concept of modern computing—the stored-program architecture where instructions and data share the same memory space—was directly derived from Turing's theoretical machine.
events.why_it_matters_en: This paper fundamentally defined the mathematical limits of computation. The Turing machine serves as the conceptual ancestor for all subsequent programming languages, operating systems, and microprocessor architectures. By establishing that a universal machine could simulate any other computing machine through a set of instructions, Turing laid the absolute groundwork for software and hardware separation. Without this theoretical breakthrough, the development of modern computers—and by extension, the entire field of artificial intelligence—would not have been possible.

events.title_zh: Turing Bombe 在布莱切利园首次部署
events.title_en: Turing Bombe First Deployed at Bletchley Park
events.summary_zh:
1940 年 3 月 18 日，由艾伦·图灵设计、英国制表机公司（BTM）Harold “Doc” Keen 团队制造的第一台 Bombe 机器（绰号 “Victory”）在布莱切利园 1 号小屋正式投入运行，用于破译德军 Enigma 密码机。
Bombe 通过同时模拟多台 Enigma、用 “crib”（已推测出的明文片段）反向搜索转子设置，把数百万种可能性压缩到可以在数小时内穷举的范围。
events.behind_scenes_zh:
图灵的设计直接建立在波兰密码学家 Marian Rejewski 1938 年发明的 bomba 之上——Rejewski 团队 1932 年就破解了早期 Enigma，1939 年 7 月战争爆发前把成果传给英法。
图灵的关键贡献是意识到德军已改用更复杂的指示系统，必须改用基于消息文本（而非指示过程）的搜索法。
1940 年 8 月，第二台机器 “Agnus Dei”（Agnes）加入 Gordon Welchman 发明的 diagonal board，利用 Enigma 插线板的对称性把候选解进一步压缩约 26 倍——这是把 Bombe 从“勉强能用”变成“决定战局”的关键改进。
整个战争期间共约有 200 台 Bombe 在运行，约 2,000 名 WRNS（妇女皇家海军服务团）的 Wren 成员担任操作员。
events.why_it_matters_zh:
Bombe 是机器大规模介入符号推理的最早实战之一。
它把密码破译从人力脑算推进到机电并行搜索——这条思路后来在 AI 的搜索、约束满足、推理引擎里反复出现。
理解 Bombe，图灵就不止是“图灵测试”的代名词，也是站在现代计算与智能机器前夜的人。
events.source_name: Bletchley Park Trust - Bombe History / TNMOC Bombe Rebuild
events.card_summary_zh: Bombe 通过同时模拟多台 Enigma、用 “crib”（已推测出的明文片段）反向搜索转子设置；Bombe 是机器大规模介入符号推理的最早实战之一。
events.card_summary_en: The Bombe simulated multiple Enigma machines simultaneously to reverse-engineer rotor settings using guessed plaintext fragments known as cribs. This marked one of the earliest practical applications of machines in large-scale symbolic reasoning.
events.summary_en: Designed by Alan Turing and built by Harold "Doc" Keen's team at the British Tabulating Machine Company (BTM), the first Bombe machine—nicknamed "Victory"—was officially deployed in Hut 1 at Bletchley Park to decipher German Enigma communications. The electromechanical device worked by simulating multiple Enigma machines simultaneously. Using guessed plaintext fragments known as "cribs," it reverse-engineered the Enigma's rotor settings, compressing millions of possible configurations into a manageable range that could be exhaustively searched within hours.
events.context_en: Turing's design built directly upon the bomba invented in 1938 by Polish cryptologist Marian Rejewski, whose team had cracked early Enigma codes in 1932 and shared their findings with British and French intelligence just before the war broke out in July 1939. Turing's crucial contribution was recognizing that as the German military adopted more complex indicator systems, decryption required a search method based on the message text itself rather than the indicator process. In August 1940, a second machine named "Agnus Dei" (Agnes) incorporated the diagonal board invented by Gordon Welchman. This addition exploited the symmetry of the Enigma plugboard to further reduce candidate solutions by a factor of 26, a critical improvement that transformed the Bombe from a marginal tool into a decisive asset. Throughout the war, approximately 200 Bombes were in operation, run by around 2,000 members of the Women's Royal Naval Service (Wrens).
events.why_it_matters_en: The Bombe represents one of the earliest practical deployments of machines for large-scale symbolic reasoning. It advanced cryptanalysis from human mental calculation to electromechanical parallel search—a conceptual approach that would later repeatedly appear in AI search algorithms, constraint satisfaction problems, and inference engines. Understanding the Bombe highlights that Alan Turing was not merely the namesake of the Turing Test, but a foundational figure standing at the dawn of modern computing and intelligent machinery.
events.source_author: Bletchley Park Trust - Bombe History / TNMOC Bombe Rebuild (institutional record)

events.title_zh: McCulloch-Pitts 神经元：神经活动的逻辑演算
events.title_en: McCulloch-Pitts Neuron: A Logical Calculus of Nervous Activity
events.summary_zh:
1943 年，神经生理学家 Warren McCulloch 和 20 岁的自学逻辑学家 Walter Pitts 发表 《A Logical Calculus of the Ideas Immanent in Nervous Activity》（Bulletin of Mathematical Biophysics, 5: 115–133）。
他们把神经元抽象为一个简单的二值逻辑单元：接收多个兴奋性输入和抑制性输入，当兴奋性输入之和超过阈值且无抑制性输入时，神经元发放一个全或无的脉冲。
这种抽象让神经系统第一次可以用命题逻辑的形式语言来描述。
events.behind_scenes_zh:
Pitts 是这段合作里更传奇的一方：他 12 岁在芝加哥图书馆读 Russell 的《数学原理》，发现错误后写信给 Russell，被 Russell 邀请去剑桥（因家境贫寒未成行），15 岁在芝加哥大学图书馆遇到 Carnap，用自己读出的笔记纠正 Carnap 的逻辑符号，被 Carnap 默默安排旁听研究生课。
1942 年 McCulloch 在芝加哥认识 Pitts，把他接到家里住下，两人通宵讨论“大脑能否用逻辑描述”。
论文的核心论点是：任何能用有限神经元网络实现的功能，都等价于某个命题逻辑表达式，反之亦然——这是“大脑即计算机”假说的最早数学化版本，也是图灵机思想在神经网络语境下的对应物。
events.why_it_matters_zh:
它是神经网络研究的第一块积木，把“机器模拟神经系统”从哲学命题拉到可计算模型。
后来的感知机、反向传播、深度学习都复杂得多，但都沿着“连接 + 信号 + 阈值”这条线生长。
McCulloch 和 Pitts 还影响了 von Neumann 1945 年 EDVAC 报告里的“神经元类比”电路设计。
events.source_name: Bulletin of Mathematical Biophysics, 5:115-133 / Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy
events.card_summary_zh: 他们把神经元抽象为一个简单的二值逻辑单元：接收多个兴奋性输入和抑制性输入，当兴奋性输入之和超过阈值且无抑制性输入时。
events.card_summary_en: Warren McCulloch and Walter Pitts abstracted the biological neuron into a simple binary logic unit, firing an all-or-nothing pulse when the sum of excitatory inputs exceeds a threshold without inhibitory interference.
events.summary_en: In 1943, neurophysiologist Warren McCulloch and 20-year-old self-taught logician Walter Pitts published "A Logical Calculus of the Ideas Immanent in Nervous Activity" in the Bulletin of Mathematical Biophysics. They abstracted the biological neuron into a simple binary logic unit that receives multiple excitatory and inhibitory inputs. When the sum of excitatory inputs surpasses a specific threshold—and no inhibitory inputs are present—the neuron fires an all-or-nothing pulse. This foundational abstraction allowed the nervous system to be described using the formal language of propositional logic for the very first time.
events.context_en: Walter Pitts brought a legendary background to this collaboration. At age 12, he read Bertrand Russell's Principia Mathematica in a Chicago library, spotted errors, and wrote to Russell, who invited him to Cambridge (an offer Pitts could not accept due to poverty). At 15, he met Rudolf Carnap at the University of Chicago library and corrected Carnap's logical notation using his own notes, prompting Carnap to quietly arrange for him to audit graduate courses. In 1942, McCulloch met Pitts in Chicago and invited the young logician to live with his family. The two spent nights debating whether the brain could be described through logic. Their resulting paper argued a core thesis: any function computable by a finite network of neurons is equivalent to a propositional logic expression, and vice versa. This represented the earliest mathematical formalization of the "brain as a computer" hypothesis, effectively serving as the neural network equivalent of the Turing machine concept.
events.why_it_matters_en: The McCulloch-Pitts neuron served as the foundational building block for neural network research, transforming the philosophical concept of machine-simulated nervous systems into a computable mathematical model. While subsequent developments like the perceptron, backpropagation, and modern deep learning are vastly more complex, they all evolved along this original trajectory of connections, signals, and thresholds. Furthermore, McCulloch and Pitts's work directly influenced John von Neumann's 1945 First Draft of a Report on the EDVAC, shaping the "neuron analogy" used in early electronic circuit design and bridging the gap between biological inspiration and digital computing.

events.title_zh: von Neumann《EDVAC 报告初稿》：存储程序架构的起源
events.title_en: First Draft of a Report on the EDVAC
events.summary_zh:
1945 年 6 月 30 日，John von Neumann 完成《First Draft of a Report on the EDVAC》，由 ENIAC 项目安全官 Herman Goldstine 誊成 101 页打字稿并复印约 24 份分发给 EDVAC 项目核心成员（von Neumann 手写了原稿，Goldstine 据此誊写）。
这份打字稿首次系统描述了“存储程序”架构：把程序指令和数据都以数字形式存进同一个可寻址、可重写的内存，中央算术单元（CA）、中央控制单元（CC）、内存（M）、输入（I）、输出（O）五大部件分工明确。
这就是后来被称为“冯·诺依曼架构”的现代计算机基础结构。
events.behind_scenes_zh:
von Neumann 在普林斯顿与 Los Alamos 之间往返的火车上手写这份草稿，邮寄回费城。
他当时与 ENIAC 设计者 Eckert 和 Mauchly 紧密合作——后来 Eckert 和 Mauchly 都主张存储程序架构最初是他们提出的，但因 von Neumann 是唯一署名者，架构被冠以“冯·诺依曼”之名，这是计算机史上最有争议的署名问题之一。
草稿的电路设计部分（“E-elements”）明显受 1943 McCulloch-Pitts 神经元模型启发——von Neumann 在后来的信件与著述中明确承认这一影响（收信人姓名待核实）。
1946 年 Moore School Lectures 把这份草稿的思想传给剑桥的 Maurice Wilkes，Wilkes 回英国后造出 EDSAC（1949 年 5 月首跑），成为第一台全尺寸实用存储程序计算机。
events.why_it_matters_zh:
没有存储程序架构，就没有可运行的“AI 软件”。
EDVAC 报告第一次让“程序作为数据”变得工程可行——AI 后来的所有训练循环、模型权重、强化学习 reward signal、Transformer 的注意力矩阵，都依赖“内存里同时放数据和指令”这一前提。
报告里受 McCulloch-Pitts 启发的 E-elements 设计，也是计算神经科学与计算机架构的最早技术连接。
events.source_name: Moore School / Computer History Archive (Knuth Collection)
events.card_summary_zh: 这份打字稿首次系统描述了“存储程序”架构：把程序指令和数据都以数字形式存进同一个可寻址、可重写的内存；没有存储程序架构，就没有可运行的“AI 软件”。
events.card_summary_en: This typescript provided the first systematic description of the stored-program architecture, storing both program instructions and data digitally in a single addressable, rewritable memory. Without this architecture, executable AI software would not exist.
events.summary_en: On June 30, 1945, John von Neumann completed the First Draft of a Report on the EDVAC. Herman Goldstine, the ENIAC project's security officer, typed von Neumann's handwritten notes into a 101-page document, distributing about 24 copies to core EDVAC members. This typescript provided the first systematic description of the stored-program architecture, storing program instructions and data digitally in the same addressable, rewritable memory. It defined five major components: central arithmetic (CA), central control (CC), memory (M), input (I), and output (O). This foundational structure for modern computing became known as the von Neumann architecture.
events.context_en: Von Neumann drafted this manuscript by hand during train rides between Princeton and Los Alamos, mailing the notes back to Philadelphia. He was working closely with ENIAC designers J. Presper Eckert and John Mauchly. Eckert and Mauchly later claimed they had originally proposed the stored-program architecture, but because von Neumann was the sole listed author, the architecture was named after him—making this one of the most controversial attribution disputes in computer history. The draft's circuit design section ("E-elements") was clearly inspired by the 1943 McCulloch-Pitts neuron model, an influence von Neumann explicitly acknowledged in later letters and writings (though the specific recipient's name still needs verification). In 1946, the Moore School Lectures transmitted these ideas to Maurice Wilkes at Cambridge. Wilkes returned to the UK and built the EDSAC (which first ran in May 1949), creating the first full-scale, practical stored-program computer.
events.why_it_matters_en: Without the stored-program architecture, executable AI software would not exist. The EDVAC report made the concept of "programs as data" engineeringly feasible for the first time. All subsequent AI training loops, model weights, reinforcement learning reward signals, and Transformer attention matrices rely on the fundamental premise of storing both data and instructions simultaneously in memory. Furthermore, the report's McCulloch-Pitts-inspired "E-elements" design represents the earliest technical connection between computational neuroscience and computer architecture.
events.source_author: Moore School / Computer History Archive (institutional record)

events.title_zh: ENIAC 公开宣告：第一台通用电子数字计算机
events.title_en: ENIAC Public Announcement
events.summary_zh:
1946 年 2 月 14 日，宾夕法尼亚大学 Moore 电机工程学院公开宣告 ENIAC（Electronic Numerical Integrator and Computer）建造完成。
这台由 John Mauchly 和 J. Presper Eckert 领导设计的机器重 30 吨、占地 167 平方米、含 17,468 个真空管和 5 百万个焊点，能在一秒内完成 5,000 次加法或 357 次乘法——比当时最快的机电机器快约 1,000 倍。
ENIAC 是历史上第一台通用电子数字计算机：可重编程解决任意可计算问题，且全程电子化、无机械运动部件。
events.behind_scenes_zh:
ENIAC 项目由美军弹道研究实验室资助，最初目的是计算火炮弹道表——战时一台手摇计算器算一条弹道轨迹要数小时，前线的炮兵表更新跟不上。
Mauchly 1942 年提出电子计算方案，1943 年与 Eckert 共同立项，1945 年底完工，首次实际任务是 1945 年 12 月为 Los Alamos 国家实验室计算氢弹可行性（不在公开宣告里提及）。
ENIAC 的最大短板是“编程”——要重新设置任务，需用插线板和电缆手动改线，一次复杂的弹道设置需要两名操作员花 2~3 天插拔线缆。
正是这个痛点直接催生了 EDVAC 的存储程序架构（1945 年的 First Draft）。
ENIAC 的 6 名首席程序员全是女性（Kathleen “Kay” McNulty、Betty Snyder Holberton、Marlyn Wescoff、Ruth Lichterman、Frances Bilas、Jean Jennings Bartik），她们的编程方法论为现代软件工程奠定了基础，但直到 1990 年代才被广泛承认。
events.why_it_matters_zh:
AI 作为“软件”的可能性，建立在通用电子计算机的可用性之上。
ENIAC 证明了真空管电子计算在工程上的可行性，它的问题（重编程难）直接推动了 EDVAC 的存储程序架构、EDVAC 又被 Manchester Baby 验证、被 EDSAC 实用化——这条链路是 AI 诞生的硬件前提。
events.source_name: Computer History Museum timeline — 1946
events.card_summary_zh: ENIAC 公开宣告：第一台通用电子数字计算机；AI 作为“软件”的可能性，建立在通用电子计算机的可用性之上。
events.card_summary_en: The public announcement of ENIAC introduced the world's first general-purpose electronic digital computer. Its availability established the foundational hardware necessary for artificial intelligence to eventually emerge as software.
events.summary_en: On February 14, 1946, the Moore School of Electrical Engineering at the University of Pennsylvania publicly announced the completion of ENIAC (Electronic Numerical Integrator and Computer). Designed under the leadership of John Mauchly and J. Presper Eckert, the 30-ton machine occupied 167 square meters and contained 17,468 vacuum tubes. It could perform 5,000 additions or 357 multiplications per second—roughly 1,000 times faster than contemporary electromechanical machines. ENIAC was the first general-purpose electronic digital computer in history: it was fully electronic with no moving mechanical parts, and it could be reprogrammed to solve any computable problem.
events.context_en: Funded by the U.S. Army's Ballistic Research Laboratory, ENIAC was originally commissioned to calculate artillery firing tables. During wartime, calculating a single trajectory with a manual calculator took hours, causing critical delays for frontline artillery. John Mauchly proposed an electronic computing solution in 1942, and the project was formally initiated with J. Presper Eckert in 1943. Completed in late 1945, ENIAC's first actual task was calculating the feasibility of the hydrogen bomb for Los Alamos National Laboratory in December 1945—a classified mission omitted from the public announcement. ENIAC's primary limitation was its programming process. Reconfiguring the machine for a new task required manually changing cables on plugboards; a complex ballistic setup could take two operators two to three days to wire. This specific bottleneck directly inspired the stored-program architecture of the EDVAC (outlined in the 1945 First Draft). Notably, ENIAC's six primary programmers were all women: Kathleen "Kay" McNulty, Betty Snyder Holberton, Marlyn Wescoff, Ruth Lichterman, Frances Bilas, and Jean Jennings Bartik. Their methodological approaches laid the groundwork for modern software engineering, though their contributions were not widely recognized until the 1990s.
events.why_it_matters_en: The conceptualization of artificial intelligence as software fundamentally relied on the availability of general-purpose electronic computers. ENIAC proved the engineering viability of vacuum-tube electronic computing. Furthermore, its severe reprogramming limitations directly catalyzed the development of EDVAC's stored-program architecture. This architecture was subsequently verified by the Manchester Baby and made practical by the EDSAC. This direct lineage of hardware evolution established the essential physical prerequisites that made the eventual birth of AI possible.
events.source_author: University of Pennsylvania ENIAC Archives / IEEE Milestones (institutional record)

events.title_zh: Wiener《Cybernetics》出版：动物与机器的控制与通信
events.title_en: Norbert Wiener Publishes Cybernetics
events.summary_zh:
1948 年，Norbert Wiener 的《Cybernetics: Or Control and Communication in the Animal and the Machine》由巴黎 Hermann 出版社和纽约 John Wiley & Sons 出版（MIT Press 版本是 1961 年第二版）。
书名取自希腊语 κυβερνήτης（舵手），Wiener 把它定义为“在动物和机器中关于控制与通信的研究领域”。
全书核心论点：神经系统、社会机构、自动机器、电子电路都遵循同一套反馈控制原理，可用统计学、信息论、微分方程统一描述。
events.behind_scenes_zh:
Wiener 与 Bigelow、Rosenblueth 1943 年的论文是这本书的思想源头。
1943–1944 年 Wiener 和计算机先驱 John von Neumann、神经生理学家 Warren McCulloch 共同发起 Macy 基金会赞助的跨学科会议（后称 “Macy Cybernetics Conferences”），1946–1953 年共举办 10 届，常客包括 von Neumann、McCulloch、Pitts、Rosenblueth、Margaret Mead、Gregory Bateson、Heinz von Foerster 等。
这场会议直接催生了认知科学（cognitive science）——1956 年 MIT 的 Symposium on Information Theory 和 Dartmouth AI Conference 的多位参与者都来自 Macy 圈子。
Wiener 自己后来与 AI 圈决裂：1956 年他拒绝参加 Dartmouth 会议，认为军事化研究违背控制论的伦理初衷。
events.why_it_matters_zh:
它给 AI 时间轴补上前史根系。
今天谈 Agent、机器人、自动化工作流、强化学习时，仍能看到反馈回路和控制循环的影子。
1956 年 Dartmouth 会议为这门新学科命名时，“cybernetics（控制论）”也是备选之一，最终选了 “artificial intelligence”，但两者思想重叠极深。
events.source_name: Hermann / Wiley 1948 / Britannica - Cybernetics
events.card_summary_zh: 书名取自希腊语 κυβερνήτης（舵手），Wiener 把它定义为“在动物和机器中关于控制与通信的研究领域”；给 AI 时间轴补上前史根系。
events.card_summary_en: Deriving its name from the Greek word for "steersman," Norbert Wiener defined cybernetics as the study of control and communication in animals and machines, establishing the prehistory of artificial intelligence.
events.summary_en: In 1948, Norbert Wiener published Cybernetics: Or Control and Communication in the Animal and the Machine (jointly published by Hermann in Paris and John Wiley & Sons in New York, with the MIT Press edition following in 1961). Taking its name from the Greek word kybernētēs (steersman), Wiener defined the field as the study of control and communication in animals and machines. The book's core thesis argued that nervous systems, social institutions, automated machines, and electronic circuits all operate on identical principles of feedback control, which can be uniformly described using statistics, information theory, and differential equations.
events.context_en: The ideological origins of the book trace back to a 1943 paper co-authored by Wiener, Julian Bigelow, and Arturo Rosenblueth. Between 1943 and 1944, Wiener, computer pioneer John von Neumann, and neurophysiologist Warren McCulloch initiated interdisciplinary meetings sponsored by the Macy Foundation. Known as the Macy Cybernetics Conferences, ten sessions were held from 1946 to 1953, featuring regular attendees like von Neumann, McCulloch, Walter Pitts, Rosenblueth, Margaret Mead, Gregory Bateson, and Heinz von Foerster. These conferences directly catalyzed the emergence of cognitive science; many participants at the 1956 MIT Symposium on Information Theory and the Dartmouth AI Conference originated from the Macy circle. However, Wiener later broke ties with the nascent AI community. He refused to attend the 1956 Dartmouth Conference, believing that the militarization of such research violated the original ethical intentions of cybernetics.
events.why_it_matters_en: Cybernetics provides the foundational prehistory of the AI timeline. The concepts of feedback loops and control cycles introduced by Wiener remain highly visible today in discussions surrounding AI agents, robotics, automated workflows, and reinforcement learning. When the Dartmouth Conference convened in 1956 to name this new discipline, "cybernetics" was considered as a primary candidate. Although the organizers ultimately selected "artificial intelligence," the ideological overlap between the two fields remains profound, cementing Wiener's work as a critical precursor to modern AI.

events.title_zh: Manchester Baby：首台存储程序电子计算机运行
events.title_en: The Manchester Baby (SSEM) Executes the World's First Stored Program
events.summary_zh:
1948 年 6 月 21 日下午，曼彻斯特大学的小型实验机器（Small Scale Experimental Machine，昵称 “Baby”）首次成功运行程序：Tom Kilburn 写的代码寻找 2^18 = 262,144 的最大因数，在 52 分钟内跑完约 350 万次运算并给出正确答案 131,072（指令数常见引用为约 3.5 million operations，精确数字待核实）。
这是人类历史上第一次让“程序本身”作为数据存进电子存储器、被电子方式读取并执行。
Baby 的存储器是 Freddie Williams 和 Tom Kilburn 联合发明的 Williams-Kilburn Tube（阴极射线管存储器），用单根 6 英寸 CRT 存下 2048 位——这是当时世界范围内最有效的随机存取电子存储器。
events.behind_scenes_zh:
Williams 1946 年 7 月在英国 Malvern 的电信研究院（TRE）开始研究 CRT 存储，1946 年 12 月调到曼彻斯特大学，把 Kilburn 也带过去继续合作，Geoff Tootill 1947 年 6 月加入协助。
到 1947 年 12 月 1 日，他们已经能在单根 CRT 上稳定存储 2048 位，并写了一份被英美广泛传阅的内部报告。
Baby 的本意是测试 Williams-Kilburn Tube 能否在电子速度下读写任意位，但既然要造一台机器来测试存储器，他们就顺手把存储程序架构也验证了。
1951 年 2 月 Ferranti 公司基于 Manchester Mark I（Baby 的后继）推出 Ferranti Mark I，成为世界上第一台作为标准产品交付给客户的商用电子计算机。
events.why_it_matters_zh:
AI 能成为程序、模型、系统，前提是机器能运行可更换的程序。
存储程序架构让“软件”这个概念有了物理载体——程序不再是改线路、插线缆，而是改内存里的数据。
1986 年 IEEE 把 Baby 列为国际里程碑，认定它是“第一台执行存储程序的电子计算机”。
events.source_name: University of Manchester Digital60 / IEEE Milestones
events.card_summary_zh: Manchester Baby：首台存储程序电子计算机运行；AI 能成为程序、模型、系统，前提是机器能运行可更换的程序。
events.source_author: University of Manchester Digital60 / IEEE Milestones (institutional record)
events.card_summary_en: The Manchester Baby became the first electronic computer to run a stored program. This foundational breakthrough established that machines could execute interchangeable software, a prerequisite for modern AI models and systems.
events.summary_en: On the afternoon of June 21, 1948, the University of Manchester's Small-Scale Experimental Machine (nicknamed "Baby") successfully ran its first program. Written by Tom Kilburn to find the highest proper factor of 2^18, the program ran for 52 minutes, executing approximately 3.5 million operations (the precise number still needs verification) to output the correct answer. This marked the first time a program was stored as data in electronic memory and executed electronically. The machine utilized the Williams-Kilburn Tube, a cathode-ray tube memory co-invented by Freddie Williams and Tom Kilburn, storing 2,048 bits on a single 6-inch CRT—then the world's most effective random-access electronic memory.
events.context_en: Freddie Williams began researching CRT memory at the Telecommunications Research Establishment (TRE) in Malvern, UK, in July 1946. He transferred to the University of Manchester in December 1946, bringing Tom Kilburn with him to continue their collaboration. Geoff Tootill joined to assist them in June 1947. By December 1, 1947, the team could stably store 2,048 bits on a single CRT, documenting their success in an internal report that circulated widely across the UK and the US. The original purpose of the Baby was simply to test whether the Williams-Kilburn Tube could read and write arbitrary bits at electronic speeds. However, since they needed to build a machine to test the memory anyway, they took the opportunity to validate the stored-program architecture simultaneously. In February 1951, Ferranti introduced the Ferranti Mark I, based on the Manchester Mark I (the Baby's successor). This became the world's first commercially available electronic computer delivered to a customer as a standard product.
events.why_it_matters_en: The ability of AI to exist as programs, models, and systems is fundamentally predicated on machines being able to run interchangeable software. The stored-program architecture provided a physical foundation for the concept of software. Programming no longer required rewiring circuits or plugging in cables; instead, it simply meant altering data within memory. In 1986, the IEEE recognized the Baby as an international milestone, officially designating it as the first electronic computer to execute a stored program.

events.title_zh: Shannon《A Mathematical Theory of Communication》发表
events.title_en: Shannon's Mathematical Theory of Communication
events.summary_zh:
1948 年 7 月和 10 月，Claude Shannon 在 Bell System Technical Journal 分两期发表 《A Mathematical Theory of Communication》。
论文首次给出“信息”的严格数学定义——信息量等于事件发生概率的对数倒数（H = -Σ p log₂ p），单位是 bit——这个词由同事 John Tukey 提出，Shannon 在本文中首次将其引入印刷文献。
他证明任何通信信道都有一个上限（信道容量 C = W log₂(1+S/N）），并给出 “source coding” 和 “channel coding” 分离定理：压缩和传输可以独立优化而不损失整体最优性。
events.behind_scenes_zh:
Shannon 1937 年在 MIT 的硕士论文《A Symbolic Analysis of Relay and Switching Circuits》首次把布尔代数应用到电路设计——Howard Gardner 后来称之为“20 世纪最重要的硕士论文”。
1941 年 Shannon 加入贝尔实验室，参与战时密码工作（与 Turing 在纽约贝尔实验室有过交流，具体地点待核实），对通信、加密、噪声的思考最终汇成 1948 年的论文。
1949 年 Shannon 与 Warren Weaver 合作出书，书名改为《The Mathematical Theory of Communication》——从“A Mathematical”（一种）变成“The Mathematical”（唯一），标志着信息论从一门“可能的工具”升格为“已确立的学科”。
events.why_it_matters_zh:
AI 处理的文字、图像、语音、代码本质上都是信息。
信息论让 AI 有了量化“不确定性”和“表示”的工具：决策树用信息增益选择分裂特征、交叉熵是分类损失函数的标准选择、VAE 的 ELBO 含 KL 散度、Transformer 的注意力可视为软性信息检索——这些今日深度学习的基础构件，都可以回到 Shannon 1948 年的 H 公式。
events.source_name: Bell System Technical Journal 27(3):379-423, 27(4):623-656 / IEEE
events.card_summary_zh: 他证明任何通信信道都有一个上限（信道容量 C = W log₂(1+S/N））；AI 处理的文字、图像、语音、代码本质上都是信息。
events.card_summary_en: Claude Shannon proved that any communication channel has a theoretical upper limit for data transmission. Ultimately, the text, images, audio, and code processed by modern AI are fundamentally forms of information.
events.summary_en: In July and October 1948, Claude Shannon published "A Mathematical Theory of Communication" in two parts in the Bell System Technical Journal. The paper provided the first rigorous mathematical definition of information, quantifying it as the negative logarithm of probability (H = -Σ p log₂ p) and measuring it in "bits"—a term coined by colleague John Tukey and first introduced to print here. Shannon proved that any communication channel has a maximum capacity (C = W log₂(1+S/N)) and introduced the separation theorem for source and channel coding, demonstrating that data compression and transmission can be optimized independently without losing overall efficiency.
events.context_en: Shannon's 1937 master's thesis at MIT, A Symbolic Analysis of Relay and Switching Circuits, was the first to apply Boolean algebra to electrical circuit design—a work Howard Gardner later called the most important master's thesis of the 20th century. In 1941, Shannon joined Bell Labs and contributed to wartime cryptography. During this period, he interacted with Alan Turing at Bell Labs in New York (though the exact location of their meetings remains to be verified). His deep reflections on communication, encryption, and noise ultimately culminated in his landmark 1948 paper. In 1949, Shannon co-authored a book with Warren Weaver, slightly altering the title to The Mathematical Theory of Communication. The shift from "A" to "The" was highly symbolic, marking the elevation of information theory from a potential analytical tool to a firmly established scientific discipline.
events.why_it_matters_en: The text, images, audio, and code processed by modern AI are fundamentally forms of information. Information theory provided AI with the mathematical tools to quantify uncertainty and representation. Many foundational components of contemporary machine learning rely directly on these concepts: decision trees use information gain to select splitting features, cross-entropy is the standard choice for classification loss functions, the ELBO in Variational Autoencoders incorporates KL divergence, and Transformer attention mechanisms can be viewed as soft information retrieval. All of these fundamental building blocks of modern deep learning trace their theoretical roots back to Shannon's 1948 entropy formula.

events.title_zh: Hebb《The Organization of Behavior》：突触可塑性假说
events.title_en: Hebb's The Organization of Behavior
events.summary_zh:
1949 年，加拿大心理学家 Donald Hebb 在 McGill 大学出版《The Organization of Behavior》。
他提出一个后来被概括为 “Hebb's rule” 的假说：“当细胞 A 的轴突足够接近细胞 B 并反复参与其激发时，A 到 B 的连接会被增强”——通俗表述是 “Cells that fire together, wire together”（一起激发的神经元会连接得更强）。
这是“学习 = 突触强度变化”这一神经网络核心思想的最早系统化陈述。
events.behind_scenes_zh:
Hebb 写这本书的直接动机是反驳 Karl Lashley 的 “mass action” 学说——Lashley 通过切除大鼠皮层不同区域的实验，认为大脑皮层是均质的、整体参与的，没有功能定位。
Hebb 不同意，他自己在蒙特利尔做的大鼠学习实验显示，特定细胞群的活动模式确实会随学习改变。
Hebb 在书里还提出 “cell assembly”（细胞集合）概念：一组反复共同激发的神经元会形成稳定回路，这些回路就是记忆和概念的物理基础。
这套思想启发了 1958 Rosenblatt 的感知机、1982 Hopfield 网络、1973 年 Bliss 与 Lømo 发现的 Long-Term Potentiation (LTP)——LTP 被证实是真实突触层面的 Hebbian 机制。
events.why_it_matters_zh:
Hebb 法则让“学习”在神经层面有了“连接强度变化”的物理基础。
后来的反向传播、Spike-Timing-Dependent Plasticity (STDP）、脉冲神经网络，尽管数学复杂得多，但核心画面仍是“经验改变连接”。
它也是生物学和 AI 互相借鉴的最古老桥梁之一。
events.source_name: Wiley 1949 / Britannica - Donald O. Hebb
events.card_summary_zh: 他提出后来被概括为“Hebb 法则”的假说：当两个神经元反复一起活跃时，它们之间的连接会增强。这个“一起激发、一起连接”的规则，为神经层面的学习给出了最早的物理解释。
events.card_summary_en: Donald Hebb proposed what became known as Hebb's rule, suggesting that repeated neural firing strengthens synaptic connections. This hypothesis provided a physical basis for learning through changes in connection strength.
events.summary_en: In 1949, Canadian psychologist Donald Hebb published The Organization of Behavior while at McGill University. He proposed a hypothesis that later became known as Hebb's rule: when the axon of cell A is near enough to excite cell B and repeatedly takes part in firing it, the connection between the two is strengthened. Often summarized as "cells that fire together, wire together," this was the earliest systematic statement of a core neural network concept—that learning equates to changes in synaptic strength.
events.context_en: Hebb’s direct motivation for writing the book was to refute Karl Lashley’s theory of "mass action." Based on experiments involving the ablation of different cortical areas in rats, Lashley argued that the cerebral cortex was homogeneous and functioned as a whole, without localized functions. Hebb disagreed; his own rat learning experiments in Montreal indicated that the activity patterns of specific cell groups did indeed change with learning. In his book, Hebb also introduced the concept of the "cell assembly," proposing that a group of neurons repeatedly firing together would form a stable circuit, serving as the physical basis for memories and concepts. This framework profoundly influenced later developments, inspiring Frank Rosenblatt’s Perceptron in 1958 and the Hopfield network in 1982. Furthermore, it anticipated the 1973 discovery of long-term potentiation (LTP) by Tim Bliss and Terje Lømo, which confirmed that Hebbian mechanisms operate at the level of actual biological synapses.
events.why_it_matters_en: Hebb's rule provided a physical foundation for learning at the neural level, defining it as a change in connection strength. While later mechanisms like backpropagation, spike-timing-dependent plasticity (STDP), and spiking neural networks are mathematically much more complex, their core paradigm remains rooted in the idea that experience alters connections. This hypothesis stands as one of the earliest and most enduring bridges between biological neuroscience and artificial intelligence, establishing a foundational breakthrough for modern neural networks.
events.source_author: Wiley 1949 / Britannica - Donald O. Hebb (institutional record)

events.title_zh: Turing《Computing Machinery and Intelligence》：图灵测试的起源
events.title_en: Computing Machinery and Intelligence
events.summary_zh:
1950 年 10 月，Alan Turing 在哲学期刊《Mind》第 59 卷第 236 期发表《Computing Machinery and Intelligence》（pp. 433-460）。
文章开头拒绝直接定义“机器”和“思考”，转而提出“模仿游戏”（imitation game）：如果一台机器在通过电传打字机进行对话时，能让提问者难以判断对方是人还是机器，是否就应当承认它能“思考”？
这就是后来被称作“图灵测试”（Turing Test）的思想实验。
Turing 在文中预测：到 2000 年，一台 10⁹ 位存储的计算机能在 5 分钟测试中骗过 30% 的裁判。
events.behind_scenes_zh:
Turing 此时刚在曼彻斯特大学 Ferranti Mark 1 上班。
他写这篇文章的真正对手是当时英国哲学界盛行的“机器不可能思考”论调，尤其是神经学家 Geoffrey Jefferson 1949 年的演说——“没有机器能因思考而写出一首十四行诗”。
Turing 在文章里逐一驳斥 9 个反对意见（神学、鸵鸟、数学、意识、各种能力），最后用儿童程序类比作结：与其写一个成人程序，不如写一个能学习的儿童程序让它自己长大。
这个观点直接预示了今天 LLM pretrain → fine-tune → RLHF 的范式。
当代数学家 Chris Bernhardt 在《Turing's Vision》（2016）中指出，Turing 真正的核心论点是“可计算等价”——人类思维若是某种计算，机器早晚能做到。
events.why_it_matters_zh:
这篇文章把“机器能不能思考”这个无法用定义解决的哲学问题，改写为“机器能否在行为上表现到与人难以区分”这个可观察、可比较的操作问题。
今天所有 chatbot benchmark、对话评测、AGI 评判标准——无论 LLM 红蓝对抗、Elo 排名还是图灵测试复刻——本质上都是这条思路的延续。
events.source_name: Mind, vol. LIX, no. 236, pp. 433-460 (October 1950)
events.card_summary_zh: 文章开头拒绝直接定义“机器”和“思考”，转而提出“模仿游戏”（imitation game）。
events.card_summary_en: Bypassing the philosophical debate over defining "machine" and "thought," Alan Turing proposed the "imitation game," laying the conceptual groundwork for evaluating machine intelligence.
events.summary_en: In October 1950, Alan Turing published "Computing Machinery and Intelligence" in the philosophical journal Mind. Rather than attempting to define "machine" or "think," Turing introduced the "imitation game." He proposed that if a machine communicating via a teleprinter could fool an interrogator into believing it was human, it should be considered capable of thought. This thought experiment became known as the Turing Test. Turing also predicted that by the year 2000, a computer with 10⁹ bits of storage would be able to deceive 30% of human judges during a five-minute test.
events.context_en: At the time of publication, Turing had recently begun working on the Ferranti Mark 1 at the University of Manchester. His primary target was the prevailing sentiment in British philosophy that machines could not think, exemplified by neurologist Geoffrey Jefferson's 1949 assertion that no machine could write a sonnet through genuine thought. In the paper, Turing systematically refuted nine common objections to machine intelligence, ranging from theological arguments to arguments from consciousness and mathematical limitations. He concluded by suggesting that rather than attempting to program a fully formed adult mind, researchers should build a "child machine" capable of learning and growing. This concept directly foreshadowed the modern paradigm of pre-training, fine-tuning, and reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) used in today's large language models. As contemporary mathematician Chris Bernhardt noted in Turing's Vision (2016), Turing's core argument was ultimately about computational equivalence: if human thought is a form of computation, machines will eventually be able to replicate it.
events.why_it_matters_en: Turing's paper fundamentally transformed the unanswerable philosophical question of whether machines can think into an observable, operational metric: whether a machine's behavior is indistinguishable from a human's. By shifting the focus from internal consciousness to external performance, Turing established the foundational framework for evaluating artificial intelligence. Today, every chatbot benchmark, conversational evaluation, and proposed standard for artificial general intelligence (AGI)—from LLM red-teaming and Elo rating systems to modern iterations of the Turing Test itself—is essentially a continuation of this pragmatic approach.
events.source_author: Mind, vol. LIX, no. 236, pp. 433-460 (institutional record)

events.title_zh: McCarthy-Minsky-Rochester-Shannon 提案："Artificial Intelligence" 一词的首次正式使用
events.title_en: A Proposal for the Dartmouth Summer Research Project on Artificial Intelligence
events.summary_zh:
1955 年 8 月 31 日，John McCarthy、Marvin Minsky、Nathaniel Rochester（IBM 701 总设计师）和 Claude Shannon 联名向洛克菲勒基金会提交了《A Proposal for the Dartmouth Summer Research Project on Artificial Intelligence》（打字稿，页数待核实）。
提案建议 1956 年夏在达特茅斯学院举办为期 2 个月、10 人参与的“人工智能”暑期研讨会。
这是 “Artificial Intelligence” 一词第一次出现在正式学术文档中。
提案核心论断：“学习的每一个方面、智能的任何特征，原则上都可以被精确描述到机器能够模拟的程度”。
events.behind_scenes_zh:
McCarthy 当时是达特茅斯学院的数学助理教授，27 岁。
他想组织一个暑期研讨会，但不知道取什么名字——“cybernetics” 被 Wiener 强烈把持（且 Wiener 与 McCarthy 关系紧张）；
“automata theory” 太数学化；
“complex information processing” 太工程化。
他最终选择 “artificial intelligence”，部分原因是为了避开 Wiener——Wiener 当时已是 MIT 名教授，他若反对任何人用 “cybernetics” 都有杀伤力。
提案四作者中，Rochester 代表 IBM 的硬件资源，Shannon 代表信息论的合法性，Minsky 代表神经科学背景，McCarthy 自己代表数学逻辑背景——这个组合让提案既有工程落地又有理论分量，最终从洛克菲勒基金会拿到 7,500 美元（远低于申请金额，具体申请数额待核实）。
events.why_it_matters_zh:
这份提案不只是为 AI 命名，更是为整个领域划定了研究范围——语言、抽象、问题求解、自我改进，这些主题到 2020 年代仍是 AI 的核心议题。
McCarthy 后来回忆：“我之所以选 “artificial intelligence” 这个名字，是因为它中立——不偏向 Wiener 的 cybernetics（模拟反馈），也不偏向 automata theory，还能避开与 Norbert Wiener 的争论”。
events.source_name: McCarthy, Minsky, Rochester, Shannon (1955). A Proposal for the Dartmouth Summer Research Project on Artificial Intelligence.
events.card_summary_zh: 提案建议 1956 年夏在达特茅斯学院举办为期 2 个月、10 人参与的“人工智能”暑期研讨会。
events.card_summary_en: This proposal suggested a two-month, ten-person summer research project on "artificial intelligence" at Dartmouth College, marking the first official use of the term.
events.summary_en: John McCarthy, Marvin Minsky, Nathaniel Rochester (chief architect of the IBM 701), and Claude Shannon submitted "A Proposal for the Dartmouth Summer Research Project on Artificial Intelligence" to the Rockefeller Foundation. The typed manuscript (page count pending verification) proposed a two-month, ten-person summer workshop at Dartmouth College for 1956. This marked the first appearance of the term "artificial intelligence" in a formal academic document. The proposal's core assertion was that "every aspect of learning or any other feature of intelligence can in principle be so precisely described that a machine can be made to simulate it."
events.context_en: At the time, John McCarthy was a 27-year-old assistant professor of mathematics at Dartmouth College. He wanted to organize a summer workshop but struggled to name the field. "Cybernetics" was heavily dominated by Norbert Wiener (with whom McCarthy had a strained relationship), "automata theory" sounded too mathematical, and "complex information processing" was too engineering-focused. McCarthy ultimately chose "artificial intelligence" partly to avoid Wiener, a prominent MIT professor whose opposition to others using "cybernetics" could have been highly damaging. The proposal's four authors formed a strategic alliance: Rochester brought IBM's hardware resources, Shannon provided the legitimacy of information theory, Minsky contributed a neuroscience background, and McCarthy offered mathematical logic. This combination gave the proposal both engineering practicality and theoretical weight, ultimately securing $7,500 from the Rockefeller Foundation (a sum significantly lower than requested, though the exact requested amount still needs verification).
events.why_it_matters_en: This proposal did more than just name artificial intelligence; it delineated the foundational research scope for the entire field. By identifying themes such as language, abstraction, problem-solving, and self-improvement, the authors established a research agenda that remains central to AI even in the 2020s. McCarthy later recalled that he chose the term "artificial intelligence" for its neutrality—it did not lean toward Wiener's cybernetics (which focused on analog feedback) or automata theory, and crucially, it allowed the emerging discipline to avoid direct ideological conflicts with Norbert Wiener.

events.title_zh: Dartmouth 暑期 AI 研讨会：人工智能作为学科的诞生
events.title_en: Dartmouth Summer Research Project on Artificial Intelligence: The Birth of the Field
events.summary_zh:
1956 年 6 月 18 日至 8 月 17 日（约 8 周，据 Ray Solomonoff 当年笔记），Dartmouth Summer Research Project on Artificial Intelligence 在新罕布什尔州汉诺威的达特茅斯学院召开。
McCarthy、Minsky、Shannon、Rochester 四人为组织者，实际参与者包括 Ray Solomonoff、Oliver Selfridge、Trenchard More、Arthur Samuel、Allen Newell、Herbert Simon、John Holland 等。
这是 “Artificial Intelligence” 第一次作为正式学科名称出现，被普遍视为 AI 学科的诞生事件。
events.behind_scenes_zh:
会议组织松散，原计划 10 人全程参加，实际只有 McCarthy、Minsky、Solomonoff 三人常驻，其他人在不同周来访——Newell 和 Simon 只来了前两周（且未现场演示 Logic Theorist，而是远程报告）。
Solomonoff 在会上首次提出“算法概率”（algorithmic probability），这是后来 Kolmogorov 复杂度、Solomonoff 归纳、AIXI 的源头。
Trenchard More 接替 Rochester 在第三周到访，记录了大量笔记。
会议虽未达成原计划的“突破性集体成果”，但确立了“符号 vs 神经”“逻辑 vs 概率”的分野——1956 之后，符号派（CMU Newell-Simon、MIT Minsky-McCarthy）占据主流 30 年，直到 1980s 反向传播复兴神经网络，2012 AlexNet 让神经派重新主导。
Solomonoff 晚年回忆：“we didn't solve any big problem that summer, but we agreed on the name—and the name mattered.”
events.why_it_matters_zh:
Dartmouth 把分散在 cybernetics、automata theory、complex information processing 等不同名号下的研究首次汇拢为统一学科，并明确核心问题：自动计算机、自然语言、神经网络、计算理论、抽象与创造、自我改进。
这些主题在 70 年后仍是 AI 的研究主线。
会议也催生了之后 20 年 AI 的主要研究力量——MIT、CMU、Stanford、IBM 四大机构的 AI 实验室几乎都由 Dartmouth 参与者创办。
events.source_name: Solomonoff, R. (1956) Dartmouth notes; McCarthy 1956 attendee list to Rockefeller Foundation
events.card_summary_zh: 一群数学家与计算机科学家第一次把“人工智能”当作共同研究目标，一个新学科由此获得名字。
events.card_summary_en: A group of mathematicians and computer scientists gathered to establish "artificial intelligence" as a shared research goal, officially giving the new discipline its name.
events.summary_en: Held at Dartmouth College in Hanover, New Hampshire, the Dartmouth Summer Research Project on Artificial Intelligence ran for approximately eight weeks. Organized by John McCarthy, Marvin Minsky, Claude Shannon, and Nathaniel Rochester, the workshop brought together researchers including Ray Solomonoff, Oliver Selfridge, Trenchard More, Arthur Samuel, Allen Newell, Herbert Simon, and John Holland. This event marked the first time "artificial intelligence" was used as an official academic term, and it is widely recognized as the founding event of AI as a distinct scientific discipline.
events.context_en: The workshop was loosely organized. Although originally planned for ten full-time attendees, only McCarthy, Minsky, and Solomonoff stayed for the entire duration, while others visited during different weeks. Newell and Simon attended only the first two weeks, presenting their Logic Theorist remotely rather than demonstrating it on-site. During the event, Solomonoff first proposed "algorithmic probability," which later became the foundation for Kolmogorov complexity, Solomonoff induction, and the AIXI model. Trenchard More replaced Rochester in the third week and kept extensive notes. While the gathering did not achieve its planned foundational breakthrough as a collective output, it established the enduring divides between symbolic and neural approaches, as well as logic and probability. Following 1956, the symbolic school—led by Newell and Simon at CMU, and Minsky and McCarthy at MIT—dominated the field for 30 years. This paradigm held until the 1980s revival of neural networks via backpropagation and the 2012 AlexNet breakthrough that restored the neural approach to prominence. As Solomonoff recalled in his later years: "We didn't solve any big problem that summer, but we agreed on the name—and the name mattered."
events.why_it_matters_en: The Dartmouth workshop consolidated disparate research efforts previously scattered across cybernetics, automata theory, and complex information processing into a unified discipline. It explicitly defined core challenges that remain central to AI research decades later: automatic computers, natural language, neural networks, theory of computation, abstraction and creativity, and self-improvement. Furthermore, the event catalyzed the primary research forces that would drive AI for the next 20 years. The foundational AI laboratories at MIT, CMU, Stanford, and IBM were almost entirely established by participants of the Dartmouth summer project.

events.title_zh: General Problem Solver（GPS）：首个目标导向的通用问题求解器
events.title_en: General Problem Solver
events.summary_zh:
1957 年，Allen Newell、Cliff Shaw、Herbert Simon 在 RAND Corporation 提出通用问题求解器 GPS。
GPS 不像 Logic Theorist 只能证明逻辑定理，而是用“手段-目的分析”（means-ends analysis）把任意问题分解为：当前状态、目标状态、可用算子、差异检测——通过不断“减小当前状态与目标状态之间的差异”来搜索解法。
该程序在 JOHNNIAC 上实现，能解逻辑定理、不定式积分、传教士与食人族过河等多种问题。
events.behind_scenes_zh:
GPS 的真正突破不在算法本身，而在“把人解题的思维过程变成机器算法”这个方法论。
Newell 和 Simon 在 1956-1957 大量观察人类被试“出声思考”，记录他们解逻辑题时的思维链——“我想先看看结论跟假设差在哪，然后找一个能减少这个差异的规则”——再把这种思维模式抽象为算法。
这种“protocol analysis”方法论后来成为认知科学的标准工具。
GPS 的失败也很重要：它只能处理“中等难度”问题，一旦状态空间指数爆炸就无能为力——这个限制在 1965-1975 让整个 GPS 路线陷入困境，也是 1972 年 Dreyfus《What Computers Can't Do》批评的主要靶子。
1980 年代专家系统转向“窄而深”（如 MYCIN 只做血液感染）就是 GPS 通用路线失败的产物。
events.why_it_matters_zh:
GPS 是历史上第一个明确以“通用”为目标的 AI 程序，确立了“问题=状态空间搜索”这个后来统治 AI 30 年的范式。
手段-目的分析至今仍是规划、调度、自动化推理系统的基本思路。
Newell 和 Simon 1975 年图灵奖颁奖词中明确把 GPS 列为主要贡献。
events.source_name: Newell, A., Shaw, J. C., Simon, H. A. (1959). Report on a general problem-solving program. Proceedings of the International Conference on Information Processing, 256-264.
events.card_summary_zh: General Problem Solver（GPS）：首个目标导向的通用问题求解器。
events.card_summary_en: The General Problem Solver (GPS) was the first goal-directed AI program designed to solve a variety of problems using a generalized approach.
events.summary_en: In 1957, Allen Newell, Cliff Shaw, and Herbert Simon introduced the General Problem Solver (GPS) at the RAND Corporation. Unlike the Logic Theorist, which was limited to proving logical theorems, GPS utilized "means-ends analysis" to decompose arbitrary problems. It defined a current state, a goal state, available operators, and difference detection, searching for solutions by continuously reducing the gap between the current and goal states. Implemented on the JOHNNIAC computer, GPS could solve various tasks, including logical theorems, indefinite integrals, and the Missionaries and Cannibals puzzle.
events.context_en: The true breakthrough of GPS lay not in its algorithm, but in its methodology of translating human cognitive processes into machine algorithms. Between 1956 and 1957, Newell and Simon extensively observed human subjects "thinking aloud," recording their chains of thought as they solved logic puzzles. They noted how subjects identified differences between conclusions and assumptions, then sought rules to reduce those gaps, and subsequently abstracted this cognitive pattern into an algorithm. This "protocol analysis" methodology later became a standard tool in cognitive science. However, the limitations of GPS were equally significant. It could only handle problems of moderate difficulty and failed when faced with the exponential explosion of state spaces. This constraint stalled the GPS trajectory between 1965 and 1975 and became a primary target of Hubert Dreyfus's 1972 critique, *What Computers Can't Do*. The 1980s shift toward "narrow and deep" expert systems, such as MYCIN for blood infections, was a direct response to the failure of the generalized GPS approach.
events.why_it_matters_en: GPS was the first AI program explicitly designed with the goal of general-purpose problem solving. It established the paradigm of framing problems as state-space searches, an approach that dominated artificial intelligence for the next 30 years. Furthermore, its core mechanism of means-ends analysis remains a fundamental concept in modern planning, scheduling, and automated reasoning systems. The development of GPS was explicitly cited as a major contribution when Newell and Simon were awarded the Turing Award in 1975.
events.source_author: A. Newell, J. C. Shaw, H. A. Simon

events.title_zh: Rosenblatt 感知机：可学习神经网络的首次实现
events.title_en: Rosenblatt's Perceptron
events.summary_zh:
1957 年 Frank Rosenblatt 在纽约 Buffalo 的 Cornell Aeronautical Laboratory（CAL）首次在 IBM 704 上仿真感知机算法（Project PARA），用 50 次训练让机器学会区分打孔卡的左标记与右标记——这是历史上第一次机器通过自身调整权重从例子中学习。
1958 年 7 月，美国海军研究办公室（ONR）在 CAL 公开演示，Rosenblatt 同年发表《The Perceptron: A Probabilistic Model for Information Storage and Organization in the Brain》（Psychological Review, 65(6), 386-408）。
1960 年 6 月 23 日，Mark I Perceptron 硬件演示——400 个光电管+512 个 association unit+8 个 response unit+电动可调电位器构成第一台可学习的物理神经网络机器。
events.behind_scenes_zh:
Rosenblatt 在 Bronx High School of Science 读高中，比同校低一年级的 Marvin Minsky 早一年。
两人在 1950s 末就开始了感知机 vs 符号 AI 的争论——Minsky 在 1969 年与 Seymour Papert 合著《Perceptrons》用 XOR 反例证明单层感知机无法学习线性不可分问题，这本书被广泛认为是引发第一次 AI 寒冬的导火索。
但近年的史学研究发现 Minsky-Papert 的批评被过度解读——他们自己也在书末讨论多层网络的可能性，且 Rosenblatt 当时已在研究多层网络（只是未找到有效训练算法）。
真正的瓶颈是反向传播算法尚未成熟——Rosenblatt 死前 4 年，他高中同学 Minsky 在写书打击他的研究路线，而他本人在尝试从训练老鼠大脑提取物质注射给未训练老鼠这种“生物机器学习”实验。
这段历史是 AI 学科最戏剧性的篇章之一。
2021 年 IEEE 为 Rosenblatt 颁发 Computer Pioneer Award（追授）。
events.why_it_matters_zh:
感知机是历史上第一个能“从经验中学习”的程序化机器，确立了“输入-权重-激活-误差-更新”这个至今仍是神经网络基本框架的范式。
它直接启发 1960s Widrow 的 Adaline、1980s 反向传播、2010s 深度学习——今天 PyTorch 的 nn.Linear 本质上仍是 Rosenblatt 的感知机。
Rosenblatt 1971 年 43 岁生日当天死于帆船事故，未能看到反向传播复兴。
events.source_name: Rosenblatt, F. (1958). The Perceptron: A Probabilistic Model for Information Storage and Organization in the Brain. Psychological Review, 65(6), 386-408.
events.card_summary_zh: 感知机第一次让机器根据样本自行调整权重，今天神经网络“从数据中学习”的基本轮廓由此出现。
events.card_summary_en: The perceptron allowed a machine to adjust its own weights based on training samples for the first time, establishing the foundational paradigm of neural networks learning from data.
events.summary_en: In 1957, Frank Rosenblatt simulated the perceptron algorithm (Project PARA) on an IBM 704 at the Cornell Aeronautical Laboratory (CAL). After 50 training cycles, the machine learned to distinguish left and right marks on punch cards, marking the first time a machine learned from examples by adjusting its own weights. Following a public demonstration by the US Office of Naval Research in July 1958, Rosenblatt published his seminal paper on the model. By June 1960, the Mark I Perceptron hardware was demonstrated, utilizing 400 photocells, 512 association units, and motorized potentiometers to create the first learnable physical neural network machine.
events.context_en: Frank Rosenblatt and Marvin Minsky attended the Bronx High School of Science together, with Rosenblatt one year senior. By the late 1950s, the two were already debating the merits of perceptrons versus symbolic AI. In 1969, Minsky and Seymour Papert published Perceptrons, using the XOR problem to prove that single-layer perceptrons could not learn linearly inseparable functions. This book is widely cited as a catalyst for the first AI winter. However, recent historical research suggests their critique was over-interpreted: Minsky and Papert discussed the potential of multi-layer networks in the book's conclusion, and Rosenblatt was already researching them, though he lacked an effective training algorithm like backpropagation. In a dramatic chapter of AI history, while Minsky was writing the book that would severely impact neural network research, Rosenblatt was conducting 'biological machine learning' experiments, attempting to transfer memory by injecting brain extracts from trained rats into untrained ones. The IEEE posthumously awarded Rosenblatt the Computer Pioneer Award in 2021.
events.why_it_matters_en: The perceptron was the first programmable machine capable of learning from experience. It established the 'input-weight-activation-error-update' paradigm that remains the foundational framework for neural networks today. This foundational breakthrough directly inspired Bernard Widrow's ADALINE in the 1960s, the backpropagation revival of the 1980s, and the deep learning boom of the 2010s. In fact, the standard linear layers used in modern frameworks like PyTorch are essentially direct descendants of Rosenblatt's perceptron. Tragically, Rosenblatt died in a boating accident on his 43rd birthday in 1971, never living to see the eventual triumph of the neural network architecture he pioneered.

events.title_zh: McCarthy 在 MIT 启动 Lisp：早期 AI 的母语诞生
events.title_en: McCarthy Begins Lisp Development at MIT
events.summary_zh:
1958 年秋，John McCarthy 离开达特茅斯到 MIT 任助理教授，与 Marvin Minsky 共同组建 MIT Artificial Intelligence Project。
McCarthy 试图用 IBM 704 上的 FORTRAN 处理 AI 列表操作（FLPL: FORTRAN List Processing Language），但发现 FORTRAN 缺少递归、条件表达式、动态内存分配——他决定发明一门新语言。
1958 年圣诞节至 1959 年初，他在 MIT 一个人的寒假里写出《Recursive Functions of Symbolic Expressions and Their Computation by Machine, Part I》草稿，首次定义 S-表达式、λ-演算、条件表达式、垃圾回收、eval 元循环解释器——这门语言被命名为 Lisp（LISt Processing）。
1959 年他的学生 Steve Russell 读完论文后说：“等等，eval 是可以直接跑的”，于是把 McCarthy 纸上的伪代码敲进 IBM 704——Lisp 第一个真正运行的解释器由此诞生。
1960 年 4 月论文正式发表于 Communications of the ACM。
events.behind_scenes_zh:
McCarthy 在《History of Lisp》（1979 年 Stanford 报告）里回忆，Lisp 的诞生有两个关键意外——第一是 “S-表达式”：他最初设计的是 M-表达式（类似 FORTRAN），但 M-表达式很难解析，他被迫用 S-表达式（嵌套括号）做底层表示，结果 S-表达式天然同构于语法树，反而成了 Lisp 的核心优势。
第二是 “垃圾回收”：早期 IBM 704 内存只有 32K 字，列表对象频繁分配/释放，程序员手动管理极易出错，McCarthy 被迫发明 mark-and-sweep 算法自动回收——这是计算机科学史上第一次系统提出垃圾回收概念。
McCarthy 还设计了 Advice Taker（1958-1959 提案）——一个用逻辑声明常识、能自己推理的程序，他举的例子：“告诉机器“鸟会飞”，它就应推出“麻雀会飞”，除非你告诉它“企鹅不会飞””。
Advice Taker 直接启发了 Prolog（1972 Colmerauer）、Cyc（1984 Lenat）和今天的 prompt engineering——LLM 的 system prompt 本质就是 McCarthy 当年想象的“advice”。
McCarthy 1971 年获图灵奖。
2011 年 10 月 24 日去世，84 岁，去世前几天还在改论文《What is common sense and how to give it to machines?》。
events.why_it_matters_zh:
Lisp 是 AI 历史上最重要的一门语言。
代码即数据（homoiconicity）、垃圾回收、高阶函数、REPL、宏、闭包——几乎所有现代编程语言核心特性都来自 Lisp。
Python、JavaScript、Ruby、Rust、Clojure、Julia 都在还 Lisp 的债。
更关键的是，Lisp 的元循环 eval 直接启发了Prolog 解释器、1970s 专家系统 shell、2010s LLM 的 token-by-token 解码——凡涉及“程序操纵程序”的地方几乎都能看到 Lisp 的影子。
events.source_name: McCarthy, J. (1960). Recursive Functions of Symbolic Expressions and Their Computation by Machine, Part I. Communications of the ACM, 3(4), 184-195.
events.card_summary_zh: 1959 年他的学生 Steve Russell 读完论文后说：“等等，eval 是可以直接跑的”；Lisp 是 AI 历史上最重要的一门语言。
events.card_summary_en: After reading McCarthy's paper, his student Steve Russell realized the theoretical eval function could be implemented directly in code. This breakthrough helped establish Lisp as a foundational programming language in AI history.
events.summary_en: In the fall of 1958, John McCarthy joined MIT and co-founded the MIT Artificial Intelligence Project with Marvin Minsky. Finding that FORTRAN on the IBM 704 lacked recursion and dynamic memory allocation for AI list operations, McCarthy invented a new language. Over the winter break, he drafted a paper defining S-expressions, garbage collection, and the eval meta-circular evaluator for Lisp (LISt Processing). When his student Steve Russell realized the theoretical eval function could be executed, he programmed McCarthy's pseudocode into the IBM 704, creating the first working Lisp interpreter. The foundational paper was formally published in 1960.
events.context_en:
In his 1979 Stanford report History of Lisp, McCarthy recalled two key accidents in the language's creation. First, he initially designed FORTRAN-like M-expressions but found them difficult to parse. He was forced to use nested-bracket S-expressions for the underlying representation, which naturally mapped to syntax trees and became Lisp's core advantage. Second, because the early IBM 704 had only 32K words of memory, manual management of frequently allocated list objects was error-prone. This compelled McCarthy to invent the mark-and-sweep algorithm for automatic memory management—the first systematic conceptualization of garbage collection in computer science history.

During this period, McCarthy also proposed the Advice Taker (1958–1959), a program designed to use logical declarations of common sense to reason independently. He envisioned telling a machine that "birds can fly," allowing it to deduce that "sparrows can fly" unless explicitly told that penguins cannot. The Advice Taker directly inspired later systems like Prolog and Cyc, and its conceptual framework mirrors modern prompt engineering, where an LLM's system prompt functions much like McCarthy's imagined "advice." McCarthy, who won the Turing Award in 1971, passed away in 2011 at age 84, spending his final days editing a paper on imparting common sense to machines.
events.why_it_matters_en: Lisp stands as one of the most important programming languages in the history of artificial intelligence. It introduced foundational concepts that define modern programming, including homoiconicity (code as data), garbage collection, higher-order functions, the REPL environment, macros, and closures. Contemporary languages like Python, JavaScript, Ruby, Rust, Clojure, and Julia all owe a significant debt to Lisp's architectural innovations. Crucially, Lisp's meta-circular eval function directly inspired the Prolog interpreter, 1970s expert system shells, and the conceptual framework behind token-by-token decoding in modern large language models. Wherever computing involves programs manipulating programs, Lisp's enduring influence remains visible.

events.title_zh: Samuel《Some Studies in Machine Learning Using the Game of Checkers》："Machine Learning" 一词的首次学术定义
events.title_en: Samuel Coins "Machine Learning" in IBM Journal
events.summary_zh:
1959 年 7 月，Arthur Samuel 在《IBM Journal of Research and Development》第 3 卷第 3 期发表《Some Studies in Machine Learning Using the Game of Checkers》（pp. 210-229）。
这是 “Machine Learning” 一词首次以学术方式正式使用，后人常用“让计算机在未被显式编程的情况下学习”来概括 Samuel 的思想（此句为转述，非论文原文逐字）；Samuel 论文中的真实表述是“a computer can be programmed so that it will learn to play a better game of checkers than can be played by the person who wrote the program”。
论文系统描述了跳棋程序的两类学习：rote learning（记棋谱）和 learning by generalization（参数学习），后者实质上就是后来 Sutton & Barto 在《Reinforcement Learning》中定义的 temporal-difference learning。
events.behind_scenes_zh:
Samuel 之所以推动 “machine learning” 这个词，是因为他想区别于 “cybernetics”（被 Wiener 把持）和 “artificial intelligence”（被 McCarthy 把持）。
他在 IBM 的位置特殊——既是 Dartmouth 参与者，又长期游离于 MIT/CMU/Stanford 三大 AI 中心之外。
他选择跳棋这个看似“小”的领域深耕 30 年，实际上是为了证明“机器学习不需要先解决 AGI”——在某个领域专注训练就能达到专家级。
Samuel 的 alpha-beta 剪枝（约 1959 年与 Newell-Simon-Shaw 同期独立提出，源头归属仍有争议）和 temporal-difference 学习（被 Sutton 1988 论文正式命名）后来成为强化学习的两大基石。
Samuel 1990 年 88 岁高龄在 Stanford 工作到去世，他晚年常感叹：“我做的事人们称之为 reinforcement learning，但 1959 年我管它叫 learning by generalization”。
events.why_it_matters_zh:
这篇论文不只首次定义了 machine learning 这个学科名，也首次证明了“机器可以通过 self-play 训练到超越程序作者的水平”——Samuel 程序在 1962 年赢了自称跳棋高手的 Robert Nealey 一局（Nealey 是视障人士，但“盲棋”一词容易误指蒙眼下棋，应予澄清；此役当年被 IBM 大力宣传，次年回赛即落败），他自评：“the program can now play a better game of checkers than can be played by the person who wrote it”。
这一论断直接预示了 2017 年 AlphaGo Zero 的 self-play 超越人类知识。
Tom Mitchell 1997 年《Machine Learning》教科书定义 ML 时明确引用 Samuel 这篇论文。
events.source_name: Samuel, A. L. (1959). Some Studies in Machine Learning Using the Game of Checkers. IBM Journal of Research and Development, 3(3), 210-229.
events.card_summary_zh: 这是 “Machine Learning” 一词首次以学术方式正式使用；篇论文不只首次定义了 machine learning 这个学科名。
events.card_summary_en: Arthur Samuel formally introduced the term "machine learning" in academic literature. His landmark paper not only named the discipline but also demonstrated that a computer could learn to outperform its programmer.
events.summary_en: Arthur Samuel published "Some Studies in Machine Learning Using the Game of Checkers" in the *IBM Journal of Research and Development*. This marked the first formal academic use of the term "machine learning." While often paraphrased as enabling computers to learn without being explicitly programmed, Samuel specifically wrote that a computer could be programmed to "learn to play a better game of checkers than can be played by the person who wrote the program." The paper systematically detailed two learning methods: rote learning and learning by generalization, the latter effectively serving as the foundation for what Sutton and Barto later defined as temporal-difference learning.
events.context_en: Samuel championed the term "machine learning" partly to distinguish his work from Norbert Wiener’s "cybernetics" and John McCarthy’s "artificial intelligence." His position at IBM was unique: though a participant in the seminal Dartmouth workshop, he largely operated outside the dominant AI hubs of MIT, CMU, and Stanford. By dedicating 30 years to the seemingly narrow domain of checkers, Samuel aimed to prove that machine learning did not require solving artificial general intelligence first; focused training could achieve expert-level performance in a specific area. His implementations of alpha-beta pruning (proposed independently around 1959, though its exact origins remain debated) and temporal-difference learning (formally named by Richard Sutton in 1988) eventually became cornerstones of reinforcement learning. Samuel continued working at Stanford until his death at age 88 in 1990. In his later years, he often reflected on the evolution of the field, noting that what modern researchers called reinforcement learning was exactly what he had termed "learning by generalization" in 1959.
events.why_it_matters_en: Beyond naming the discipline, Samuel's paper provided early evidence that machines could use self-play to surpass their creators' skill levels. This was famously demonstrated in 1962 when his program defeated self-proclaimed checkers master Robert Nealey in a single game. (Though heavily promoted by IBM, Nealey—who was visually impaired—defeated the program in a rematch the following year.) Samuel concluded that "the program can now play a better game of checkers than can be played by the person who wrote it." This conceptual breakthrough directly foreshadowed the self-play mechanisms that allowed AlphaGo Zero to surpass human knowledge in 2017. Tom Mitchell later explicitly cited Samuel's paper when defining the field in his definitive 1997 *Machine Learning* textbook.

events.title_zh: DENDRAL 启动:第一个大型知识驱动专家系统
events.title_en: DENDRAL Project: First Knowledge-Intensive Expert System
events.summary_zh:
1965 年春，Edward Feigenbaum 刚加入 Stanford 任计算机系创始教员，立刻与诺奖遗传学家 Joshua Lederberg 启动 DENDRAL 项目，目标是让计算机从有机化合物的质谱图反推分子结构。
1966 年 Lederberg 拉入 Carl Djerassi（口服避孕药之父、Stanford 质谱实验室负责人）补齐化学知识。
项目持续到 1982,是史上第一个大型“知识库 + 推理机”专家系统。
核心思想——“程序的能力来自具体领域知识，而不是更聪明的推理”——被称为“知识原理”,1980 年代专家系统工业化的理论基石。
events.behind_scenes_zh:
DENDRAL 最初的设计灵感来自 Lederberg 1964 年开发的 DENDRAL 算法——穷举所有可能分子结构的生成器。
但穷举会产生天文数字候选，必须靠化学家的启发式剪枝。
Feigenbaum 的关键洞察是：把这些化学家的经验直接写进程序，而不是去模拟“科学家怎么思考”。
这个“知识 vs 推理”的取舍影响了之后 20 年 AI 路线——也埋下了 1980 年代末专家系统泡沫破裂的种子（知识获取瓶颈至今未解）。
events.why_it_matters_zh:
DENDRAL 把 AI 从“通用推理器”梦想拉回到“领域知识才是关键”的现实，直接催生了 MYCIN、XCON、PROSPECTOR 等一批 1970-80 年代专家系统。
Feigenbaum 因此被称作“专家系统之父”,1994 年获 ACM Turing Award。
“知识工程”作为职业从 DENDRAL 开始成立，今天 prompt engineer 的远祖就是 DENDRAL 的知识工程师。
events.source_name: Lindsay, Buchanan, Feigenbaum, Lederberg (1993). DENDRAL: A case study. AI Journal 61:209-261.
events.card_summary_zh: DENDRAL 把化学家的经验写成可推理的规则，第一次证明 AI 能在狭窄但真实的专业领域超过普通人。
events.card_summary_en: By encoding chemists' expertise into inferable rules, DENDRAL demonstrated for the first time that AI could outperform average humans in a narrow but real-world professional domain.
events.summary_en: In spring 1965, Stanford computer science founding faculty member Edward Feigenbaum partnered with Nobel laureate geneticist Joshua Lederberg to launch the DENDRAL project, aiming to enable computers to infer molecular structures from mass spectrometry data. In 1966, chemist Carl Djerassi joined to provide domain expertise. Running until 1982, DENDRAL became the first large-scale expert system combining a knowledge base with an inference engine. Its core philosophy—that a program's power derives from domain-specific knowledge rather than smarter reasoning—established the "knowledge principle," forming the theoretical foundation for the industrialization of expert systems in the 1980s.
events.context_en: DENDRAL's initial inspiration came from an algorithm developed by Lederberg in 1964, which acted as a generator to exhaustively list all possible molecular structures. However, this exhaustive search produced an astronomical number of candidates, requiring heuristic pruning based on chemists' expertise. Feigenbaum's critical insight was to encode this practical experience directly into the program, rather than attempting to simulate how scientists actually think. This trade-off between prioritizing knowledge over general reasoning shaped the trajectory of AI research for the next two decades. At the same time, it sowed the seeds for the collapse of the expert system bubble in the late 1980s, as the fundamental bottleneck of knowledge acquisition remains unresolved to this day.
events.why_it_matters_en: DENDRAL shifted AI research away from the dream of building general-purpose reasoners and grounded it in the reality that domain knowledge is paramount. This shift directly catalyzed a wave of expert systems in the 1970s and 1980s, including MYCIN, XCON, and PROSPECTOR. Feigenbaum earned the title "father of expert systems" and received the ACM Turing Award in 1994 for this work. Furthermore, DENDRAL established knowledge engineering as a distinct profession; the knowledge engineers of the DENDRAL era can be seen as the direct ancestors of today's prompt engineers.

events.title_zh: Weizenbaum ELIZA:第一个聊天机器人的诞生
events.title_en: ELIZA: A Computer Program for the Study of Natural Language Communication
events.summary_zh:
1965 年，Joseph Weizenbaum 在 MIT Project MAC 用 MAD-SLIP 在 IBM 7094 上写出 ELIZA,通过 CTSS 分时系统让多个用户同时与程序对话。
ELIZA 是一个平台：换不同“脚本”就变不同角色。
最有名的脚本是 DOCTOR——模仿 Rogerian 心理治疗师，用“你刚才说...”“这让你想到什么？”等反问模板把用户的话包装成回应。
1966 年 1 月 CACM 9(1):36-45 发表，ELIZA 立刻成为史上第一个被普通用户当作“懂人话”的程序。
events.behind_scenes_zh:
Weizenbaum 的本意是建一个研究人机对话的平台，不是做 chatbot。
DOCTOR 脚本是他顺手做的演示，结果反客为主——“它会跑掉，去证明一件我没想让它证明的事”。
ELIZA 的“魔法”被发现后，Bernie Cosell 在 BBN 用 Lisp 重写了一个版本，通过 ARPANET 传播到整个学术界，从此 ELIZA 和 Lisp 绑定，原版 MAD-SLIP 反被遗忘 50 年。
Weizenbaum 后来写《Computer Power and Human Reason》（1976）警告 AI 滥用，成为最早的“AI 伦理”批评者之一。
events.why_it_matters_zh:
ELIZA 第一次让“机器看起来懂你”这件事被广泛体验。
Weizenbaum 的秘书在用过 20 分钟后让他离开房间——“她不愿让 Weizenbaum 看到自己对着机器掏心掏肺”。
这种 ELIZA Effect（用户过度认同机器）至今仍是 chatbot 设计的核心议题，也是 GPT、Claude、Gemini 评测中“是否被拟人化幻觉误导”的源头。
events.source_name: Weizenbaum, J. (1966). CACM 9(1):36-45
events.card_summary_zh: ELIZA 只靠简单规则复述用户的话，却让人产生“机器理解我”的错觉，人机对话的心理效应首次显形。
events.card_summary_en: By simply rephrasing user inputs using basic rules, ELIZA created the illusion of machine comprehension, revealing the psychological effects of human-computer interaction for the first time.
events.summary_en: In 1965, Joseph Weizenbaum developed ELIZA at MIT's Project MAC, writing it in MAD-SLIP on an IBM 7094. Operating via the CTSS time-sharing system, ELIZA functioned as a platform that could adopt different personas based on specific scripts. Its most famous script, DOCTOR, simulated a Rogerian psychotherapist by using pattern matching to rephrase user statements into open-ended questions. Published in January 1966, ELIZA quickly became the first computer program that everyday users perceived as capable of understanding human language.
events.context_en: Weizenbaum originally intended ELIZA to be a research platform for studying human-computer communication, not a standalone chatbot. The DOCTOR script was merely a demonstration, but it quickly overshadowed the underlying system, leading Weizenbaum to note that the program had run away to prove something he never intended. After ELIZA's conversational capabilities were discovered, Bernie Cosell at BBN rewrote the program in Lisp. This version spread rapidly across the academic community via the ARPANET, permanently associating ELIZA with Lisp while the original MAD-SLIP implementation was largely forgotten for 50 years. Appalled by how readily people attributed human-like understanding to a simple pattern-matching script, Weizenbaum became one of the earliest critics of AI ethics. He later authored Computer Power and Human Reason (1976), warning against the misuse of artificial intelligence and the dangers of delegating human responsibilities to machines.
events.why_it_matters_en: ELIZA provided the first widespread experience of a machine appearing to understand human emotions. In a famous anecdote, Weizenbaum's secretary asked him to leave the room after just 20 minutes of using the program, unwilling to let him observe her confiding in the machine. This phenomenon—where users unconsciously project human traits and empathy onto computer programs—became known as the "ELIZA effect." Today, this psychological dynamic remains a central issue in chatbot design and serves as the foundational context for evaluating whether users are misled by anthropomorphic illusions when interacting with modern large language models like GPT, Claude, and Gemini.

events.title_zh: Zadeh 模糊集合:让数学承认“差不多”
events.title_en: Fuzzy Sets
events.summary_zh:
1965 年 6 月，Lotfi Zadeh 在《Information and Control》8(3):338-353 发表《Fuzzy Sets》。
文章定义了“模糊集合”——元素对集合的隶属度不再是 0 或 1,而是 0 到 1 之间的任意实数。
并给出并、交、补等基本运算。
Zadeh 的论点很直接：现实世界中“高”“年轻”“差不多热”这类概念本身就有渐变，经典集合论逼着机器用 0/1 二选一，反而丢掉了人类推理里最关键的灰度信息。
events.behind_scenes_zh:
Zadeh 是阿塞拜疆出生的伊朗裔美国人,1944 年移居美国，长期在 UC Berkeley 任教。
他写《Fuzzy Sets》时已是 IEEE Fellow、控制论权威，却选择挑战经典集合论的根基——这让他被西方主流数学界冷遇近 20 年。
反倒是日本和苏联接纳得最快：日本 1987 年仙台地铁用模糊控制运行至今零事故；直到 1990 年代美国才大规模跟进。
Zadeh 一直活到 2017 年 96 岁去世，亲眼看到自己的思想在 LLM 时代回潮。
events.why_it_matters_zh:
模糊集合让数学第一次承认“模糊”本身可以被精确处理。
它催生了模糊逻辑、模糊控制两大学科,1980-90 年代日本家电（松下洗衣机、三菱空调、仙台地铁）用模糊控制做出“会判断”的产品。
今天洗衣机自动称重、空调恒温、相机自动对焦都还跑着模糊控制器。
在 LLM 时代，模糊集合又以“软标签”“membership score”“token probability”等面目回来。
events.source_name: Zadeh, L. A. (1965). Information and Control 8(3):338-353
events.card_summary_zh: 模糊集合允许隶属度处在 0 与 1 之间，让机器第一次能够用数学方式处理“有点像”和“差不多”。
events.card_summary_en: Fuzzy sets allowed membership degrees to range between 0 and 1, enabling machines to mathematically process concepts like "somewhat" and "almost" for the first time.
events.summary_en: In June 1965, Lotfi Zadeh published "Fuzzy Sets" in Information and Control. The paper defined "fuzzy sets," where an element's degree of membership is no longer strictly 0 or 1, but any real number between 0 and 1. It also outlined basic operations like union, intersection, and complement. Zadeh argued that real-world concepts such as "tall," "young," or "warm" inherently involve gradations. By forcing machines into binary choices, classical set theory discarded the nuanced grayscale information crucial to human reasoning.
events.context_en: Born in Azerbaijan, the Iranian-American mathematician Lotfi Zadeh immigrated to the United States in 1944 and had a long teaching career at UC Berkeley. When he wrote "Fuzzy Sets," he was already an IEEE Fellow and a recognized authority in control theory. However, his decision to challenge the foundations of classical set theory resulted in nearly two decades of cold reception from the mainstream Western mathematical community. Conversely, Japan and the Soviet Union adopted his ideas much faster. In 1987, Japan implemented fuzzy control in the Sendai subway system, which has operated without accidents ever since. It was not until the 1990s that the United States followed suit on a large scale. Zadeh lived until 2017, passing away at 96, living long enough to see his foundational ideas echo through the era of large language models.
events.why_it_matters_en: Fuzzy sets marked the first time mathematics acknowledged that ambiguity itself could be processed precisely. This foundational breakthrough spawned the disciplines of fuzzy logic and fuzzy control. During the 1980s and 1990s, Japanese manufacturers like Panasonic and Mitsubishi used fuzzy control to create appliances capable of making judgments. Today, fuzzy controllers still power automatic weighing in washing machines, thermostat regulation in air conditioners, and autofocus in cameras. In the era of large language models, the core principles of fuzzy sets have resurfaced in concepts such as soft labels, membership scores, and token probabilities.

events.title_zh: Winograd SHRDLU:积木世界里的“理解”
events.title_en: SHRDLU: Understanding Natural Language in a Blocks World
events.summary_zh:
1968-1970 年，Terry Winograd 在 MIT 开发 SHRDLU,作为博士论文（1970 完成；论文 1971 年以 MIT AI-TR-235 正式发表）。
程序运行在 DEC PDP-6 上，用 Micro Planner + Lisp 写成，用户通过电传打字机与一个虚拟“积木世界”对话——指令 SHRDLU 把红色方块放到绿色立方体上，问“刚才你拿起的是哪个？”,SHRDLU 会回答、追问、纠正、推理。
1972 年论文以《Understanding Natural Language》出书（Academic Press),被认为是 1970 年代自然语言理解的最高成就。
events.behind_scenes_zh:
Winograd 当时 24 岁，导师是 Marvin Minsky。
SHRDLU 名字来自 ETAOIN SHRDLU——Linotype 排字机字母频率排第二行的字母序列，早年排字工人出错的“乱码占位符”。
SHRDLU 看起来像通用对话系统，其实只能在 50 个词的积木世界内工作——这是 1960 年代“微世界”路线的顶峰，也是终点。
Winograd 自己后来反思:“我们当时以为把积木世界放大就是真实世界，但真实世界没有清晰边界，没有完美对齐的语义。”——这句反思在 LLM 时代又被反复引用:GPT-4 也只是“看起来懂”的大号 SHRDLU?
events.why_it_matters_zh:
SHRDLU 第一次让一个程序看起来真的“听懂”了人话——它结合语法、语义、推理、记忆、规划，把“理解”做成可见的工程系统。
之后的 NLP 研究者要么在 SHRDLU 的路径上做小改进，要么（如 Winograd 自己）转向批评这条路:Winograd 1970 年代末转到 Stanford,转向 HCI 和 Heidegger 哲学，断言“SHRDLU 路线走不通，因为它依赖封闭世界”,这一反思影响了整个 1980-90 年代 NLP 方向。
events.source_name: Winograd, T. (1972). Understanding Natural Language. Academic Press. PhD thesis, MIT, 1970.
events.card_summary_zh: SHRDLU 能听懂指令、追踪上下文并操作虚拟积木，却也暴露了 AI 一离开封闭世界就会失灵的边界。
events.card_summary_en: SHRDLU could understand instructions, track context, and manipulate virtual blocks, but it also exposed the limitations of AI systems that fail once they leave a closed micro-world.
events.summary_en: Developed by Terry Winograd at MIT between 1968 and 1970 for his doctoral dissertation, SHRDLU was a landmark natural language understanding program. Running on a DEC PDP-6 and written in Micro Planner and Lisp, it allowed users to interact with a virtual "blocks world" via a teletypewriter. Users could instruct SHRDLU to place a red block on a green cube and then ask, "Which one did you just pick up?" The system could answer, ask clarifying questions, correct errors, and reason. Published as the book *Understanding Natural Language* in 1972, SHRDLU is widely considered the pinnacle of 1970s natural language processing.
events.context_en: Winograd was a 24-year-old graduate student advised by Marvin Minsky when he developed the system. The name "SHRDLU" derives from "ETAOIN SHRDLU," the arrangement of the most frequently used letters on a Linotype machine's keyboard, which often appeared as a placeholder or error string in early print. While SHRDLU appeared to be a general-purpose conversational system, it could only operate within a strictly defined blocks world containing a vocabulary of about 50 words. This represented both the peak and the dead end of the 1960s "micro-world" approach to AI. Winograd later reflected on this limitation, noting that researchers mistakenly believed scaling up the blocks world would equate to the real world, failing to realize that the real world lacks clear boundaries and perfectly aligned semantics. In the era of large language models, this reflection is frequently revisited, prompting debates over whether modern systems like GPT-4 are simply scaled-up versions of SHRDLU that only "appear to understand."
events.why_it_matters_en: SHRDLU was the first program that genuinely appeared to "understand" human language, successfully combining syntax, semantics, reasoning, memory, and planning into a visible engineering system. It demonstrated that natural language understanding was computationally feasible within a constrained environment. However, its ultimate legacy lies in its limitations. Subsequent NLP researchers either made incremental improvements to the SHRDLU paradigm or, like Winograd himself, fundamentally critiqued it. Moving to Stanford in the late 1970s, Winograd shifted his focus to human-computer interaction and Heideggerian philosophy, asserting that the SHRDLU approach was a dead end because it relied on a closed world. This profound realization heavily influenced the trajectory of NLP research throughout the 1980s and 1990s.

events.title_zh: Engelbart「演示之母」:NLS 与个人计算诞生
events.title_en: Douglas Engelbart's "Mother of All Demos": The NLS and the Birth of Personal Computing
events.summary_zh:
1968 年 12 月 9 日，Douglas Engelbart 在旧金山 Fall Joint Computer Conference 上做了 90 分钟演示，首次公开展示 NLS(oN-Line System):鼠标、超文本链接、实时文字编辑、屏幕窗口、视频会议、协作文档、版本控制——今天个人计算的所有核心要素。
Engelbart 远程连线 SRI 实验室，让团队现场协作编辑一份结构化文档。
演示被称作“The Mother of All Demos”——之后的 Apple Macintosh 发布（1984)、iPhone 发布（2007）都被视作它的延续。
events.behind_scenes_zh:
Engelbart 1950 年代读到 Vannevar Bush 的“As We May Think”(1945）后立志要做“memex”。
1962 年他发表《Augmenting Human Intellect: A Conceptual Framework》，拿到 ARPA 资助在 SRI 建 Augmentation Research Center。
1968 演示用了专门的调制解调器（Microwave 视频传输 + 音频回程）连到 SRI,现场 1000 多观众第一次看到“用鼠标点链接跳转”——但当时没人意识到这是未来 50 年计算的雏形。
Engelbart 生前一直觉得自己被硅谷“偷了思想但没给credit”——Apple 1979 拜访 PARC 看 Alto 时，参考的也是 Engelbart 的 NLS 思路。
events.why_it_matters_zh:
这次演示定义了“人机交互”作为独立学科的边界。
鼠标、超链接、协作编辑这些概念被 Apple、Microsoft、Tim Berners-Lee(WWW）在 1980-90 年代商业化，成为今天所有桌面和移动设备的基础。
Engelbart 选择的“放大人类智力”路线（IA）在 LLM 时代重新成为主流——Notion AI、Cursor、Copilot 都在延续 Engelbart 1968 年的设想。
events.source_name: Engelbart, D. (1968). A Research Center for Augmenting Human Intellect. FJCC.
events.card_summary_zh: Engelbart「演示之母」：NLS 与个人计算诞生；次演示定义了“人机交互”作为独立学科的边界。
events.card_summary_en: Douglas Engelbart's "Mother of All Demos" introduced the NLS, showcasing the foundational elements of personal computing. This landmark presentation effectively defined the boundaries of human-computer interaction as an independent discipline.
events.summary_en: At the Fall Joint Computer Conference in San Francisco, Douglas Engelbart delivered a 90-minute presentation that publicly debuted the NLS (oN-Line System). The demonstration showcased the computer mouse, hypertext, real-time text editing, screen windows, video conferencing, collaborative documents, and version control—the core elements of modern personal computing. By connecting remotely to the SRI laboratory, Engelbart allowed his team to collaboratively edit a structured document live on stage. Later dubbed "The Mother of All Demos," this event established a paradigm that subsequent milestones, such as the launches of the Apple Macintosh and the iPhone, would continue to build upon.
events.context_en: Engelbart's vision was heavily influenced by Vannevar Bush's 1945 essay "As We May Think," which inspired him in the 1950s to pursue the creation of a "memex" system. In 1962, he published the seminal paper "Augmenting Human Intellect: A Conceptual Framework," securing ARPA funding to establish the Augmentation Research Center at SRI.
